parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence or documented targeting is recorded, consensual male homosexual conduct was decriminalised island-wide in 2024, and fakafifine is documented as a pre-colonial gender-identity tradition valued in regional heritage. Those are documented positives. However the dossier is thin: entry/document practice, facilities, custody, care, police treatment, violence and gender-identity remedies are not documented, so silence is not safety. With no known traveller-facing exposure but also no documented working protections, the combined regime sits moderately below an acceptance-plus-protections jurisdiction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Former buggery and indecent-assault-on-males offences, formerly carrying up to ten and five years, were repealed in 2024; no trans-specific offence is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Island-wide decriminalisation in force June 2024 removes that former criminal exposure.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Repeal removes a sexuality-law lever documented as formerly available; no evidence documents its use against gender-nonconforming people.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. A sex-asymmetric age of majority (21 men, 19 women) under the 1966 act is documented but not trans-specific and not shown to affect visitors.

street_violence_police_response.protection: Fakafifine is documented as a pre-colonial gender identity described as important cultural heritage, a documented acceptance signal.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Cultural-heritage acceptance does not document police or court response to violence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No hate-crime or anti-discrimination protection covering gender identity, or its enforcement, is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of documented remedies leaves open questions about recourse if outing leads to friction, without establishing a traveller-facing exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in having friction and uncertainty, but 0.65-A documents working complaints, compensation and reliable release; those operative remedies are not documented here, so this case is not clearly above it on recourse, though it also lacks that anchor's documented stop.

0.75-C has documented recognition of matching passport markers, training and a tribunal with counsel and compensation. This dossier documents no such entry machinery, so it sits below that anchor despite no documented exposure.

0.85-B combines explicit protection, recognised nonbinary/trans documents, trained officers, body cameras and a tribunal ordering release and apology. This dossier has decriminalisation and fakafifine heritage but none of that documented protective machinery, placing it materially below 0.85.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a documented positive - 2024 decriminalisation and a valued fakafifine tradition - with no documented traveller-facing restriction on documents, facilities, custody, care, policing or violence. The main risk is uncertainty: thin data and undocumented remedies mean consequences after outing cannot be verified. Marriage non-recognition and age-of-majority asymmetry are resident-facing or non-trans-specific and do not establish visitor exposure. Hence a moderate, uncertainty-discounted score above jurisdictions with known exposures, below jurisdictions with documented working protections.
